facts.value: If you are authorized for STEM OPT, there are no employer or location restrictions; however, please choose a job that will have you work in the U.S., not in another country.
You must carry other documents to show proof of your eligibility to re-enter the U.S. such as your I-20, passport and valid F-1 visa stamp.
If you enter the U.S. on any visa other than F-1, you will lose your F-1 status and your STEM OPT will be invalidated.
The primary purpose of Post-OPT/STEM is working. Taking classes can be done as an incidental part of your stay.
If you decide to pursue a new degree program, your Post-OPT/STEM will be invalidated once you receive the new degree I-20.
You have a 60-day grace period after your Post-OPT/STEM ends to either change your visa status, transfer to another school, pursue a new degree program at ASU, or return home.
Changing your address while your STEM OPT application is pending with USCIS may cause issues with your EAD card being mailed to you correctly.

If you must change your address while your application is pending, you must update your address through your MyUSCIS account, update your address with USPS, and update your Local Address through MyASU.
You must update your address within 10 days of moving.
If your password is entered incorrectly 3 consecutive times or if you have not logged into your SEVP Portal account for 45 days or more, the account will be locked automatically.
To reset your account password, you must click on 'Reset password,' enter your ASU Public Email address and your SEVIS ID, then check your ASU email for a temporary password.

You will be able to see the status of your application when you log into your USCIS online application. You can also use your Receipt Number from your USCIS I-797A Receipt Notice to check the status on the USCIS Case Status tool.
The ISSC takes up to 7 days to process Post-OPT/STEM request.
USCIS has an average processing time of 90 days.
